title: Attention kernel compatibility resolver for shape fragmentation and mixed-precision oscillation
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Symptoms: After rolling hybrid FlashAttention v2/v3 kernel support to canary, we observed intermittent latency spikes and an elevated tail on 95/99th percentiles for multi-shape workloads and long-context prefill. Investigation shows the runtime kernel selector oscillates between a v3-optimized kernel (better throughput for certain shapes) and a v2-compatible kernel when mixed-precision thresholds and workspace allocations vary per-request. This causes extra workspace allocations, slower prefill decode handoffs, and temporary KV-cache thrashing for a subset of customers.
problem_statement: The current kernel scoring function is too sensitive to small precision/shape signals and lacks a shape-fragmentation aggregator. This leads to per-request kernel flips and prefill/decode scheduling jitter that manifests as regressions in latency-sensitive flows. We need a compatibility resolver that stabilizes decisions, respects mixed-precision constraints, and provides deterministic fallbacks under resource contention.
proposal: Implement a kernel compatibility resolver that (1) computes a per-model compatibility matrix for supported precision/layout variants, (2) aggregates incoming request shapes over short windows to detect fragmentation and prefer stable kernels for bursts, (3) introduces a hysteresis-weighted score so small transient telemetry changes do not trigger handoffs, and (4) applies conservative prefill scheduling during oscillation windows (prefer smaller-batch deterministic kernels). Add feature flags to toggle strictness and expose decision telemetry for offline analysis.
acceptance_criteria: New compatibility matrix generation CI passes for majority of open-source models
No >5% increase in median latency on canary for representative workloads
95/99th tail improves or returns to baseline within 48h of rollout compared to the regressed canary
Telemetry shows reduced kernel flip-rate and lower workspace reallocation counts
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag and run unit + integration tests in CI. 2) Deploy to internal staging with synthetic mixed-shape replay traffic for 24h. 3) Canary 5% of traffic for latency-sensitive customers with shadow logging enabled for 72h. 4) Expand to 20% if flip-rate and tail are stable; otherwise rollback. 5) Full rollout with gradual ramp and post-rollout monitoring on perf dashboards. Include automatic rollback triggers on 95/99th degradation or error-rate increase.
tests_and_metrics: Synthetic shape-fragmentation replay harness (long-context and bursty small-requests)
Shadow traffic comparison between old and new selector (flip-rate, workspace-allocs, prefill-handoff-latency)
End-to-end bench with FA2 and FA3 model variants across A100/RTX clusters
Automated regression check that asserts no more than 3% increase in token cost for canary
observability_changes: Add metrics: kernel_flip_rate, compat_matrix_selected, shape_fragmentation_score, workspace_realloc_count, prefill_handoff_duration. Tag metrics by model_name, precision, region, and customer_tier. Log deterministic decision reason codes for post-hoc analysis.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overconservative hysteresis may hurt throughput for steady-state workloads. Mitigation: Expose hysteresis parameter as feature-flagged knob and include automated perf sweep to find sweet spot per instance type. Risk: Compatibility matrix may be stale for new model variants. Mitigation: Add nightly model-compatibility calibration job and safe-fallback default to v2-compatible kernels.
implementation_notes: Key components: (A) compat matrix builder (offline + runtime cache), (B) fragmentation aggregator (windowed sketch), (C) hysteresis-weighted scorer, (D) prefill scheduler guardrail. Keep fallbacks single-path and atomic to avoid mid-request swaps. Ensure KV-cache pinning semantics preserved when switching kernels.
